text: {"features":[{"name":"Role motivation","description":"How convincingly the letter explains why the applicant wants this specific kind of work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"States interest in the job in generic terms with little explanation of why this team or problem area matters personally."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Expresses sincere interest in security or backend work but gives only broad, interchangeable reasons for applying."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Gives a clear reason for wanting the role, such as scale or security impact, but with limited personal grounding."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Connects the role to the writer's past experience, engineering values, or career direction in a way that feels specific and believable."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Delivers a memorable, deeply personal rationale that makes the move into this exact role feel strongly motivated and hard to separate from the applicant's story."}]},{"name":"Role alignment","description":"How specifically the letter connects the applicant's background to the posted responsibilities and priorities of this role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Reads mostly like a generic software or security application and barely maps experience to the posted responsibilities."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Touches one or two relevant themes from the posting but leaves major duties or required tools unaddressed."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Covers several key elements of the role at a broad level, such as security automation, Go, Python, or AI."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Explicitly aligns experience to multiple stated responsibilities, using examples that resemble the team's work."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows precise fit to the role's actual problems, including less-obvious duties such as vulnerability handling at scale, bounded agents, variant analysis, or close partnership with security engineers."}]},{"name":"Security automation insight","description":"How well the letter frames information security work as a problem of automation, scale, and safe operational leverage.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Treats security as a general good without showing understanding of why automation matters in this domain."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions automation or secure development broadly but not the operational bottlenecks it addresses."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Recognizes that automation can reduce manual security work or speed response and frames it in practical terms."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Clearly describes security work as a scaling problem, using ideas like triage, routing, bounded workflows, or lifecycle integration."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Frames the job with systems-level insight, such as multiplying expert findings across many systems, converting manual response into durable capacity, or designing auditable automation that safely extends scarce expertise."}]},{"name":"Developer enablement mindset","description":"How strongly the letter emphasizes serving downstream engineers through low-friction security tooling and better defaults.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Focuses on the applicant's own interests or technical preferences without considering the engineers who would use the tooling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Briefly mentions helping others or broad organizational impact but not as a core concern."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows awareness that the role exists to support other engineers and improve security across teams."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Emphasizes reducing friction, improving defaults, or returning expert time to others through well-designed tooling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Centers the letter on a strong builder-for-builders mindset, repeatedly framing success as making secure behavior easier for downstream developers at scale."}]},{"name":"Production engineering experience","description":"The depth of hands-on experience testing, maintaining, launching, and operating production software systems.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows only minimal qualifying production experience, usually around the lower end of the range and with limited evidence of maintained or launched systems."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows solid early-career production work, typically a few years across testing, maintenance, and launch of a small number of services."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows established production experience, often around five years or several launched services with credible day-to-day responsibility."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows substantial production depth, typically five to seven years with multiple services and evidence of keeping systems healthy after launch."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows extensive, mature production experience, usually at the high end of the sample with repeated launch, maintenance, and operational ownership of several services."}]},{"name":"Go depth","description":"The strength of evidence that Go is a central professional language for relevant backend or infrastructure work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Mentions Go only briefly as part of the stack, with no indication of depth or centrality."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Shows professional Go use but leaves unclear whether it is a major language for the applicant."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States that Go is a primary or frequent language in production work."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Makes Go a clear day-to-day implementation language for backend or infrastructure systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents Go as the dominant language behind substantial production systems that closely resemble this role's backend work."}]},{"name":"Python depth","description":"The extent of relevant Python experience shown for tooling, services, automation, or agent work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no evidence of Python experience or only implies incidental exposure."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions Python as occasional scripting or a secondary tool without production substance."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes regular Python use for tooling, automation, analysis, or prototypes."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong production-grade Python experience in services, internal platforms, or extensible tooling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents Python as a major working language used to build robust automation or agent behavior directly relevant to this role."}]},{"name":"Agentic systems design","description":"The depth of experience designing or implementing agent-based systems with explicit control and orchestration.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention agents or autonomous tooling at all."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Refers to agents or multi-step automation only vaguely, with no clear design responsibility."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes building agentic tooling at a high level, usually with some notion of orchestration or constraints."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows clear design ownership of agent systems, including how agents act, what boundaries they obey, and how surrounding infrastructure supports them."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Demonstrates sophisticated thinking about agent architecture, emphasizing bounded autonomy, auditability, interfaces, and the division of labor between agents and control systems."}]},{"name":"Applied AI experience","description":"The strength of evidence for building and operating AI or LLM-backed functionality in production settings.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of building with AI in production."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions AI interest or exposure without shipped systems or operational responsibility."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes shipping AI or LLM-backed functionality in production."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Pairs production AI work with evidence of evaluation, hardening, or awareness of failure modes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows mature operational judgment about AI systems, including when they can be trusted, how they are evaluated, and how reliability is enforced in real use."}]},{"name":"Vulnerability triage automation","description":"The relevance and depth of experience automating vulnerability intake, classification, routing, or handling workflows.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Does not mention vulnerability intake, triage, or response tooling."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions security automation generally but not direct work on vulnerability-report workflows."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes some direct involvement in automating vulnerability handling or report routing."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows substantial experience automating intake, classification, deduplication, routing, or prioritization of vulnerability reports."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents end-to-end ownership of mature vulnerability-handling automation with clear operational leverage, such as major manual-work reduction or mostly self-serve workflows."}]},{"name":"Security assessment practice","description":"The depth of hands-on experience assessing systems for security issues and following findings through remediation.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Provides no evidence of performing security assessments."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Signals security awareness or review work only in broad terms, with little sense of method."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Describes concrete assessment activities such as threat modeling, code review, or service reviews."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows hands-on assessment practice across systems or design stages, including attack-surface analysis and verification of fixes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents security assessment as a disciplined engineering capability, with structured methods, adversarial analysis, and clear follow-through to remediation."}]},{"name":"Algorithmic depth","description":"The extent to which the letter shows practical fluency with data structures and algorithms.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Gives no evidence of data-structure or algorithmic thinking."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims comfort with algorithms broadly but without a concrete example."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Offers one credible example of using a data structure or algorithm choice to improve a system."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows repeated or consequential use of algorithmic thinking to redesign performance-sensitive or complex systems."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Demonstrates standout practical algorithmic fluency, using well-chosen structures or algorithms to make previously messy or intractable problems tractable."}]},{"name":"Offensive security engagement","description":"The strength of attacker-minded practice shown through certifications, competitions, or demonstrated exploitation work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Shows no attacker-minded practice beyond general interest in security."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions light extracurricular practice or a baseline credential with limited depth."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows active engagement through recurring CTF participation or a foundational security certification."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Shows strong offensive-security evidence, such as OSCP, serious CTF participation, or sustained attacker-oriented practice."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Presents unusually strong offensive-security credibility for a software-engineering application by combining rigorous credentials with high-level competition or clearly demonstrated exploitation capability."}]},{"name":"Relevant ownership","description":"The degree to which the letter shows end-to-end responsibility for systems directly relevant to the role.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Describes mostly exposure, assisting work, or learning rather than systems the applicant personally drove."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Claims participation in relevant projects but leaves the scope of responsibility fairly unclear."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows clear responsibility for building or maintaining one or more relevant systems or tools."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Conveys end-to-end ownership of design and implementation for important security or infrastructure tooling."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows repeated ownership of strategically important systems, with language that makes the applicant a primary shaper of architecture, boundaries, and operational behavior."}]},{"name":"Impact articulation","description":"How clearly the letter explains the operational results or leverage created by the applicant's work.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Lists tasks or technologies without explaining what effect the work had."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Suggests a positive effect in generic terms but gives little sense of operational value."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"States a plausible benefit to a team or system, such as less manual work or better performance."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Clearly ties work to meaningful operational outcomes, such as hours returned, simplified workflows, or eliminated failure classes."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Consistently frames accomplishments in terms of durable leverage for teams or systems, making the scale or significance of the results easy to grasp."}]},{"name":"Claim substantiation","description":"How well the letter supports its claims with concrete examples, technical detail, and named problem contexts.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Relies mainly on self-assertion, with few concrete examples, technical details, or named problem types."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Includes some examples, but many important claims remain broad or unsupported."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Supports major claims with a few specific technologies, workflows, or problem contexts."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Consistently backs claims with concrete examples and implementation detail that make the experience feel credible."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Builds the case almost entirely through specific, technically grounded evidence, often including problem framing, solution shape, and observable consequences rather than generic self-description."}]},{"name":"Technical initiative","description":"The degree of self-directed technical work shown beyond assigned job duties, such as open source or personal projects.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Offers no meaningful evidence of technical initiative beyond assigned work."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Mentions a small side project, occasional patches, or light outside practice."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Shows steady initiative through maintained side work, regular open-source contributions, or ongoing self-directed building."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Presents substantial extra-professional technical effort, such as maintaining an open-source project or building a serious personal systems project."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Shows exceptional initiative through ambitious, sustained projects or externally used open-source work that meaningfully reinforces readiness for the role."}]},{"name":"Writing quality","description":"The overall clarity, mechanics, and professionalism of the prose.","levels":[{"score":1,"descriptor":"Contains frequent errors or awkward phrasing that materially distract from the message and weaken credibility."},{"score":2,"descriptor":"Has noticeable mistakes or clunky wording, but the overall meaning remains clear."},{"score":3,"descriptor":"Is generally clear and professional, though some errors or flat passages remain."},{"score":4,"descriptor":"Is polished, easy to follow, and professionally voiced, with only minor lapses if any."},{"score":5,"descriptor":"Is exceptionally crisp and persuasive, combining strong mechanics, flow, and tone with essentially no distraction."}]}]}
